title: Up close with the Milky Way
caption: The heart of the Milky Way above three Unit Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The crowded heart of the Milky Way, packed with gas, dust, star clusters and glowing nebulae, forms the backdrop for three of the Very Large Telescope's Unit Telescopes lined up in a row. From left to right they are Antu (UT1), Kueyen (UT2) and Melipal (UT3). In the Mapuche language these names mean the Sun, the Moon and the Southern Cross.

The VLT, run by ESO on Cerro Paranal in northern Chile, has four Unit Telescopes with 8.2-meter main mirrors, the fourth being Yepun. They usually work separately, and one of them can record objects as faint as magnitude 30 in an hour-long exposure, about four billion times fainter than the unaided eye can see.
Joined together with four movable 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes, they form the VLT Interferometer, which can see details up to 25 times finer than a single telescope.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the gas, dust and nebulae of the Milky Way's center appear in far more detail than to an observer.

explore: Inside the VLTI, beams of light meet through a system of mirrors in underground tunnels, where the path lengths over a hundred meters must match to within a tiny fraction of a millimeter. That precision lets it make images sharp enough, in principle, to tell apart a car's two headlights at the distance of the Moon.
alt: Three large telescope enclosures lined up beneath the bright, dusty central region of the Milky Way.
